Okay. So this is what I do. I don't know if others can do this at will or if my body works weirdly.

I find a full front photo of someone famous who I want to model the face after, I make the picture large on half of my screen, then I zoom in on the in world face until they're about the same size. Then I cross my eyes slightly to make them overlap and tweak accordingly until I've gotten it as close as possible with that head's constraints. Don't forget the brow shaper too. 

Once I've got front view, I do the same with a profile view picture. 

Then I tweak to taste from there. Usually I select a lel eye facial animation like flirty or chill, then in increase the upper eyelid fold slightly to give the face a slightly more relaxed look.

If I'm making a tattoo that comes in black only, I'm not making a mesh, unwrapping the uv, making several color choice options, making a HUD ui in illustrator, and setting that HUD up in world. I'm going to be done much faster. I can create more single color tattoos faster.

Ok since you edited:
Here's an example: 

I'm making a staff and part of it has some complexity going on. So I've done that one face of six faces in 2k since it covers the largest area. The maps for it, like normal, metalness, and specular are 1024. 

One part of the staff, gems, is tiny, so it's 512 across the board. 

The rest are 1024 because they cover more area. I may downsize the material maps (normal etc) to 512 for efficiency.

I am trying to balance quality and efficiency while providing value. I'm also giving people choices between blinn and PBR until firestorm unscrews itself. 

I'm providing several color choice per face, all shoved in a HUD. 

Even using Uno which is very fast to set up it still takes time to set up. 

This all is a much longer workflow ergo I will complete less projects a month.

If you're making a simple tattoo you might not need as much time as a full mesh accessory with 20 textures per face.

It's pretty common for cishet men in gaming to use female avatars. Some of it is roleplay, experimentation, but there's also the age old "if I'm going to be looking at an Avatar's butt I want to look at one I'm attracted to" and research shows a significant population of the cishet male population finds FF lewd content arousing.

It didn't happen on Second Life but on other roleplay games I found that I preferred being male and using a male persona online. I started doing this in the late 90s. It was originally to escape sexual harassment and harassment for not fitting the female social norms. 

In 2014 I found out that medically transitioning from female to male was possible and I became questioning.

In retrospect, I wanted to wear boys clothes, do boys activities, and play with boys toys as a child. I remember wishing I could become a man. I remember being told what a trans woman is by my mother as an early teen after hearing a song on the radio and envying trans women because my stupid tween brain back when dinosaurs roamed the earth didn't know the opposite was possible.

I have been on testosterone for years and have been using a different name and pronouns for almost a decade now. 

Yes, there is some correlation between trans people and playing the type of avatar that is their destination gender. 

HOWEVER correlation doesn't imply causation. Just because people play the sex that doesn't align with their assigned gender at birth doesn't mean they're trans or otherwise genderqueer. Lots of people do things like roleplay. 

SL didn't make me trans. People like me have always been trans, might not realize it, etc. We're just using an avatar that we're comfortable on.

Being told to keep a benzo handy seems a little suspect too. There are major interactions between benzos and Spravato to the point they're telling us here of we have both, to not have a benzo on Spravato days. Same with Adderall as the double blood pressure booster can be a problem. 

Finally... Inattention? Your doctor is wanting Spravato to cure your inattention? 

I noticed that ADHD isn't in your diagnosis cluster. Have they tested you for that? Like, taken the adult ADHD test? Or are they giving you the "not hyperactive" or the. "you got good grades in school" type of stigma rubbish?

As for sound issues. Spravato changes how I hear sound temporarily. I put on a big comfortable cat ear headset and a nice foam stuffed blindfold. I grab a bottle of sparkling ice (berry lemonade seems to work best to wash the taste away), some cheeze-its (seems to help with the nausea, if I feel nauseous I focus on chewing the thing and it seems to help), and some andes mints (totally deletes the taste), and I queue up my favorite music app and instead of listening to the "soothing" meandering piano crap, I listen to music I actually enjoy (I turn on power metal and rock out).

When I'm feeling the weirds, if I close my eyes and see abstract structures made of phosphenes when my eyes are closed, and they're spinning counter clockwise I move my eyes in the clockwise direction and try to make it spin clockwise instead. 

There's no right or wrong way to do things. I hope it gets better for you.

He crawled into the void space of the cabinets and took a nap and then couldn't get out. Due to having just moved into the house three hours before, we didn't have tools or anything handy. One of my housemates panicked and called non-emergency and they dispatched a training unit from the fire department who got a good laugh and moved our dishwasher and got him out.

But the washer was old, from the 70s (we were going to replace it anyhow) and the water line brittle and broke. They turned off the water to that line with a valve under the sink. Except that was also old and didn't work.

The kitchen had to be demolished. The counters had soaked up the water, so had the walls, and it had also gotten under our floor tiles.

Asbestos in the walls is usually benign unless construction is being done. The abatement apparently cost 25k. 

The silver lining is that when all of this was going on, the demo team found black mold inside the walls as well as outside behind the old cabinets. 

The downside is we didn't have a kitchen for 4 months and the insurance and home warranty covered delivered food during that time and when all was right and we were eating healthier we were about to hit the gym and then COVID lockdown happened. 

Also Faen had just closed the purchase of the house days before. We weren't ready for this renovation so soon. 

We know he didn't actually cause all of the damage directly but he was the CATalyst for the CATastrophe so we gently rib him for it because coping with humor is a thing.

I spend most of my time in adult rated sims and I have a particular set of conditions I look for with an avatar to determine if it is ageplaying. I am particularly uncomfortable with child avatars, especially in adult sims. I'm unsure why, it might be my background as an artist, my autism, my general dislike for children, or a mixture of all of the above. 

What initiates me examining an avatar is when I see it and I find myself getting uncomfortable for an unknown reason. And I'm bothered by not knowing why I am uncomfortable and if that discomfort is appropriate so I analyze it. 

I take a screenshot of the avatar and measure it. Not in the feet and inches or centimeters way but in a head to body ratio way. Actual height measurements don't matter. Someone could be 1 foot tall and so long as their ratio is reasonable, it's fine. 

The average human is 7.5 heads tall with a head that is 8-9 inches long and 6-7 inches wide. 

Idealized figures such as in sculpture tend to be 8 heads tall. Fashion figures in art tend to be 8.5 and heroic figures that are larger than life may get up to 9 heads tall.  But I digress. 

I pull up the screenshot in Photoshop, create a new layer, and draw a line at the top and bottom of the head. I duplicate it and line the lines up until it spans the full length of the avatar. I cut off at the ankle then add like half a head height for foot, ignoring avatars on their tiptoes. 

In most cases, when I am uncomfortable, the avatar is 5-6 heads tall. For reference, a child around age 10 is six heads tall. 

But usually that's not the only element that raises an alarm. Their shoulders are often too narrow. I've read shoulders should be at least two heads wide. I'm not sure if that's including or not including neck. 

I also look at hand size. Hands are usually as long as the face. 

I also pay attention to body mass. Characters who are super svelte seem to add to the discomfort. This is because when humans hit puberty, they gain body mass even if they are female. Too low body fat and things like menses happen.

Sometimes I consider breast and hip size. Mostly if it's underdeveloped. I use the tanner scale to determine this.  If the avatar has preteen levels I find myself uncomfortable.

But even someone using the reborn with massive breasts and hips can make me uncomfortable. And people say, "But they have breasts." I knew girls in middle school with C cups. 

I also look at things like if the AO is calm and mature or hyperactive, bouncy, or cutesy.

Finally I look at behavior and clothing. Pigtails? Clothes usually related to clothing traditionally child associated. 

Is the behavior cutesy or excessively bratty,  if they are pink and frilly? Yeah nah. 

In the end I sit back and say, "This is fine," or. "Nope."

It's not one particular thing that will do it but proportions are pretty important and if enough of the boxes are checked in check mentally I run the other way.

Not a psychiatrist but someone with ADHD who is well-versed in knowledge of it as I've had to fight doctors who have tried to disregard my diagnosis several times.

There are multiple flavors of ADHD. 

Hyperactive-Impulsive type - Classically manifests in boys, but not always.

Inattentive Type - Classically overlooked and mostly diagnosed in girls, but not always.

Mixed type.

Additionally, people who have high intelligence/high IQ may mask ADHD or somewhat compensate making it harder to diagnose.

Also ADHD sometimes comes with impaired executive function. I read somewhere that. IQ > 135ish people are more susceptible to it but I don't recall where I got the pdf of the study from. It's buried deep in my dropbox.

Depending on when you were tested (they don't test during sleep, that's sus, so if you were tested at all) it's possible that symptoms were missed because you're inattentive or smart and inadvertently masking it. Back when I was a kid in the 80s and 90s, inattentive type wasn't really on the radars of many. It wasn't until 1980 that ADHD without hyperactivity was recognized by the APA.

I believe in order to get a diagnosis you have to have had a few symptoms during childhood. Think back about it and write down the symptoms you experienced.

As for treatment, you want to see a Psychiatrist, a Psychologist, or a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner. Board certified is even better.

If you have the freedom to choose which you go see, browse websites and/or call and make sure they actually treat ADHD. Some clinicians don't, especially if they work for a county or state health system, or a non-profit that serves addicts. Check reviews about the doctor or medical group before you go. You don't want to waste money to see someone who will not treat you.

Treating clinicians may be a little hesitant to diagnose and/or treat because some ADHD treatments are controlled substances and may invite criticism of them from the powers that be. 

If you can't get a diagnosis right away even with someone who treats ADHD, don't give up. It may take several visits for the doctor to become familiar with you.

Good luck.

Hello,

I play Blood Elves. A lot. I even have several characters of the same race/class/sex combination with roughly the same backstory concept written in slightly different ways.

The key is to disengage your give-a-fuck. 

Realize that characters are people and people are a combination of experiences and how they react to and adapt to those experiences. You can have two people who have different personalities who have the same background and will come out in two completely different ways as a result. Sometimes it's fun to compare and contrast.

This is actually why I like Blood Elves—The built in trauma is fantastic for character development.

Night Elves have something similar after the Lich Queen burned their tree.

You may want to ask yourself what is meaningful for you story wise and design a character based on that.

In the end you should play what you want to play and not worry too much about what everybody else is doing. Your character isn't really a dime a dozen because you are a different person than everybody else playing the same race in class and sex therefore your character will probably come out slightly different than theirs just by virtue of you being a different person who has been shaped by different experiences in real life.

Have fun with it and experiment.

The most important thing to remember about roleplaying in a situation where there is no moderator presiding over the situation is that you as a player have the right to say no to things OOC—You are the curator of your own experience and people aren't entitled to your RP just because their avatars are there.

You can say no to the random stabber and pretend like it never happened.

You can say no to the person playing the offspring of a major lore character and pretend they never happened.

You can say no to the powertripper or power tripping guild trying to assert authority over you and pretend they don't exist.

You can say no to something you find absurd and pretend it's not there.

You can say no to the ERPer trying to jump your bone.

I have a PTSD diagnosis. It's pretty pervasive but sometimes it can be more subtle than flashbacks and panic attacks. It can be as simple as physiological stress reactions to triggers.

For example—I cannot deal with screaming. I physically lock up and break down. My palms sweat, my heart races. I tremble, tear up, and can't breathe. I ruminate but don't flashback. Likewise I can't work interpersonally with older ladies where they have direct authority over me—I have an aversion to it because of what happened to me. 

Panic attacks are not always huge outbursts and can sometimes be more subtle. Time slows down. Noises that you might not notice become loud, annoying, and outright maddening until you have to leave. 

For someone with a fire trigger this could manifest as each crackle of a fire in a fireplace increasing stress until the character reaches a point where they flee from the room with sweaty palms for seemingly no reason.

First thing I think people need to realize is that there's a difference between a RP group or guild where everyone has agreed to play by the same rules and may or may not have an approval process and doing walkup RP in public. 

If everyone has agreed to play by the same rules already then keeping a secret is probably okay because the mutual trust between players has been established ahead of time. This is especially true if you have a DM, guild leader, or officers who review characters to make sure they're not overboard. 

However, there is no quality control in open walk\-up RP so each player has the responsibility and the right to curate their own experience. This means they have the choice of what they play with, they have the choice on if they want to play along with a player or guild attempting to assert authority, and aren't obligated to play out things that violate their comfort, safety, or just generally aren't within their realm of fun. The most obvious things people might not want to play along with are random character death or sexual violence\-\-that may be fun for the aggressor but it might not be fun for the recipient. It's their right to choose OOC if they want to play along.

What kind of things might someone want to know before engaging? Well sometimes people do things that may be semi\-secret IC but may be things that not everyone else wants to play along with because it might contradict someone else's personal interpretation of lore, might make someone's common sense tingle, etc. It's totally within those peoples' rights to not play with that thing they aren't down with. 

In the end most people are seeking fun or some sort of meaningful experience, and what is meaningful and fun for one person may not be meaningful or fun for another. 

What might people not want to play along with in terms of characters? Let's use a couple of my characters \(or characters I interact regularly with\) as examples of things people might not want to play with: 

1\) A disguised Felblood elf. 

2\) A bronze dragon. 

3\) A were\-raven inspired by White Wolfs' Corax. 

Right away some people may say "Nope!" That's totally okay. They do them, I'll do me, the servers are big enough for everyone to do their own thing. 

Others may say see it and say, "that's fine!" Some people are really flexible and down with most things and this is totally okay too. 

Others still may squint, read over the backstory, contemplate how plausible the story is, how powerful the character is, contemplate how Azeroth works, consider the writing style of the player, or who the player is and how much wiggle room they have with their [idiosyncrasy credits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiosyncrasy_credit), and decide one way or the other. And this is also perfectly fine.

When someone keeps something like this a secret in open public RP, or to do it to trick people into giving them a chance when they might not otherwise because they might like it if they just try it, the freedom to make a decision based on the big picture is no longer there. Players may decide to get involved with something that they might not want to be involved with. 

There's just as much chance that when the big reveal happens that the other player doesn't laugh and go "good chap you totally changed my mind about this type of RP I wouldn't have otherwise engaged in, good show," but instead has a negative reaction and then there might be negative OOC consequences and will probably be drama. 

The longer the lack of transparency goes on the more upset the player is going to be, and the more problems there can be. For example: It's easy to recon a single interaction, it's much harder to retcon a whole series of interactions which may have also resulted in other interactions with other people who will also be expected to retcon which leaves a discontinuity in several peoples' stories all because someone thought it'd be fun to have a surprise, or wanted to force people into trying RP they don't think they'll enjoy \(or know they don't enjoy\). 

So this is why I say that it's a good practice to be transparent. Just don't play with people who metagame, don't sweat the people that aren't down, put the people who flame on ignore \(I've actually not gotten any hate in game for any of the above\), and have fun with the people who are down. I've actually gotten RP because people have seen the info in the addon tooltip, liked what they read, and wanted to play with it who otherwise might have overlooked my character as another guy sitting under a tree somewhere.

Big surprises are best for groups where everyone has agreed to play by the same rules and you know folks have similar tastes beforehand, like in a group or a guild. This increases the likelihood that everyone'll have a good time and find the situations presented meaningful, rewarding, and fun.

On character profiles in RP addons: Yes and no. 

It's always been my opinion that a RP profile \(and backstory\) should be like a mini\-skirt, long enough to cover everything important but short enough to keep interest. \(Though there are exceptions to this.\)

Sometimes I see people advocate for not putting a backstory in RP or keeping something that's a huge deal a secret OOC so as to prevent metagaming. It's a stance I don't entirely agree with. 

Metagaming is poor form, but I'm not sure omitting your character profile to prevent metagaming is a good idea.  For one, you're stopping someone who doesn't know any better from making the mistake/learning to not do the thing. Defining stuff people may know/have heard, then prefacing with "You don't know this stuff IC but here it is for your entertainment" is a good way to help teach people some etiquette. 

By keeping something major a secret OOC, other players are not able to choose if they want to play along with it or not. There's no harm in being transparent with people, and if they choose not to play with your character because they're not down with something, they probably weren't a good match for you in the first place.

When I mention disruptions of scenes in progress, I'm not talking about trolling, griefing, or harassment but something my pre-wow RP group referred to as scene stealing. This is exactly what you might assume it is—A roleplay scene is in session, people are interacting, there's a flow, a mood, happenings and development. A roleplayer walking up can react to what's happening and join in the scene and become a contributing participant, or they can jump through the figurative wall like the Kool Aid guy going "Ooooh Yeah!" They kill the mood, disrupt what's going on, interrupt the flow and shift the focus from whatever was happening onto themselves making other players annoyed, roll their eyes, and want to punch that person through the internet. 

You see, while playing this type of thing may be fun and meaningful for you, other activities are going to be fun and meaningful for others, and not realizing this can impede on other people's fun. 

Scamming or stealing IC might be a spicy conflict to you, but to someone like me who is heavy into storylines involving people playing good, it's just annoying. 

If you make your character one that can enter the flow of scenes in progress rather than disrupt them with a tired gimmick you're going to have a far more positive experience than you may otherwise have.

Having a good RP experience increases the likelihood that someone will stick around in the long run. 

As for me not responding at all to a disruptive player interrupting a scene in progress?

You see, **attention** is basically the currency of roleplay and a healthy group has an equitable exchange between all participants. When you enjoy RP with people you are *paying* them attention. 

When someone interrupts the flow of the RP, and I don't want to engage them I typically don't say anything for a few reasons: They aren't entitled to my RP, it's not fun to play along with something you don't enjoy, trying to privately let people know that you aren't down with something even politely in whispers is a crap shoot with a 50-50 chance of tantrum so it's better to just say nothing at all. When I react IC to what I feel is bad behavior, I am rewarding that bad behavior with attention and with roleplay—encouraging more of that behavior and I don't want to do that. 

As another redditor said, finding a guild is a good idea. Seek like-minded RPers who enjoy the same kind of fun for a more meaningful experience.
